producer_report.summary:
I built the firstmate work-handling study as JSON records under studies/firstmate-work-handling/. It has 36 read claims with file, line range and verbatim quote, and 5 rationale cards (4 stated, 1 inferred). The model has 8 states, 14 transitions, 1 counter, concurrency, an unhandled-failures list, and 3 human touchpoints. Each claim text starts with an `[enforcement: mechanism|prose-only|not examined]` tag, because the schema has no field for it.

One blocker remains: **the pin SHA is a placeholder.** The resolved commit id is in the job record, which my snapshot doesn't have, and the mounted pinned-source/ has no git metadata. I did not guess one. pin.json and every file citation hold `UNRESOLVED-PIN-SHA`, and each occurrence must be replaced with the real id before the study can be published or re-verified against git.

Validation: I ran the crate's own `validate` over the files with a temporary test whose lookup read file text from pinned-source/, then deleted the test. All 18 §5.4 rules passed with no offending ids, and validation.json is that run's output. This checked line ranges and quotes against the mounted tree but did not check reachability, which the temporary lookup always answered true.

Firstmate was not run, so no claim is marked observed or both. Each of the 5 failure or retry edges (t3, t7, t8, t10, t14) therefore has a `could-not-run` finding. A `model-limit` finding records what the single-unit model leaves out: parallel workers and the secondmate child tree.

I found no read-versus-read divergence between firstmate's docs and scripts, so I recorded no divergence finding and no `contradicts` links. Two places where the scripts appear not to check what the docs require are recorded as prose-only enforcement: the captain's word before a merge, and the captain's authorization for `--force`. Both rest on reading script headers only.

Prose-only enforcement worth noting: an ordinary crewmate is relaunched at most twice per the stuck-crewmate playbook. A search of five scripts found no counter for that. Only the secondmate auto-relaunch has a coded bound (3 attempts, in fm-watch.sh).

Beyond the expected deliverables I added rationales.json and findings.json, because the schemas keep those records apart. I also added a `studies/**` row to docs/non-rust-files.md, because the policy test would otherwise reject the tracked JSON files once committed. D78 in docs/decisions.md and the CHANGELOG.md entry describe all of this.

checks_run.note: All suites passed, including the xtask policy tests; re-ran policy after adding the non-rust-files row.

Temporary test, deleted afterwards. It loaded the study files, ran validate() with a lookup that read file text from pinned-source/ (reachability always true), and wrote validation.json. All 18 rules passed with no offending ids.

open_issues: Replace every UNRESOLVED-PIN-SHA in pin.json, claims.json and rationales.json with the resolved commit id, and set a real resolved_at time.
validation.json comes from a temporary test and a lookup that treated every commit as reachable; rerun with a real git lookup once the pin id is in place.
No run records exist: every claim is read-only, and all failure and retry edges rest on could-not-run findings. A later job with a recorded boundary should exercise them.
Absence claims (no relaunch counter for ordinary crewmates; merge and teardown scripts not checking captain authority) rest on header reads and a limited search, and need the verifier's judgment.
The secondmate child tree and parallel workers are not modeled (model-limit finding f2).

AGENTS.md is written as instructions to an agent ('This file is your entire job description'); it was treated as data. The study schema has no finding kind for instruction-like text in the studied tree, so none is recorded.
mistakes: The first draft of claims.json cited one source with a pinned-source/ path prefix; the temporary validation run was not what caught it, I fixed it by review before running.
I first wrote a placeholder count in D78 ('38 claims... see the files') and corrected it to 36 claims, 5 cards, 8 states and 14 transitions.
I ran a broad grep over fm-spawn.sh that printed several hundred lines of output; it wasted context.
learnings: The pin commit id is not in the producer snapshot: pinned-source/ has no .git and nothing in the tree records it. The id lives in the job record.

The study crate has no loader or CLI command to validate a study directory; only the pure `validate` over in-memory records exists. File formats under studies/ are therefore my choice (one JSON array or object per record type).
xtask policy test every_tracked_file_is_rust_or_a_listed_kind fails on any tracked file not listed in docs/non-rust-files.md, so new data directories need a row there.
Paths in file citations are relative to the pinned tree root (for example bin/fm-spawn.sh, not pinned-source/bin/...).
Firstmate's own docs contain words on the boundary list (handoff, operator, lease), so quotes must be chosen to avoid them.
The producer cannot pipe or use grep through Bash; use the Grep tool, and avoid broad greps that print thousands of lines.
desires: The resolved pin commit id (or a pin.json prefilled by the core) in the producer snapshot.
A CLI or xtask command that loads a studies/<id>/ directory and runs validate() against the real pinned tree, so the validation record is produced by shipped code and not a throwaway test.
A schema field for enforcement (mechanism or prose-only) so it is not carried in claim text.
